study.title: LOPA – Steel works natural gas distribution network (worked example)
study.unit: Utilities – natural gas receiving, pressure reduction and plant distribution
study.team: G. Safety (LOPA facilitator), C. Gas Network (process), E. Instrument (instrument / BMS), D. Operator (operations), F. Mechanical (regulators and valves)
study.hazopTitle: PHA / HAZOP – Natural gas distribution network (worked example)
study.hazopFile: Steel works gas network - HAZOP HZ-EX-GN-001.hazop.json
study.scope: The four HAZOP deviations ticked LOPA: PRS-1 overpressure of the MP network (N02-02), reheat furnace flame loss with gas flowing (N06-01), reverse flow of process gas into the NG line (N04-03) and oxygen in the NG line at the oxy-fuel burners (N05-01). Illustrative values for training – not design data from any real plant.

settings.basis: Typical example values – replace with the client's tolerable risk criteria before the study.

scenarios.node: N02 – Gas heaters H-1101A/B and pressure reduction station PRS-1
scenarios.deviation: PRS outlet pressure above MP design pressure (10 barg)
scenarios.consequence: Overpressure of the whole MP network (inlet up to 42 barg vs 10 barg design): flange leaks and possible rupture across the site, overpressure of district stations and burner trains – fires / explosions at several locations

ie.basis: CCPS LOPA (2001) Table 5.1 – pressure regulator failure (part of FT-GN-01 demand gate G-006)

modifiers.desc: Probability of ignition – gas release 1–50 kg/s
modifiers.basis: Cox, Lees & Ang (1990) as reproduced in Lees (2012) Table 16.72 – verify

modifiers.desc: Probability that a person is present near the MP network when it leaks
modifiers.basis: Rounds about 17 h a week – CCPS ECCM (2014) Table 3.4

ipls.name: PCV-1103A/B – Monitor regulator takes over on active-regulator failure (set 7.5 barg)
ipls.basis: FT-GN-01 gate G-004 – monitor regulator PCV-1103A fails to take over

adj.evidence: FT-GN-01 G-004; annual lock-up and take-over test records

ipls.name: SSV-1102A/B – Slam-shut valve with over-pressure shut-off (OPSO 8.5 barg) on each regulator run
ipls.basis: FT-GN-01 gate G-005 – slam-shut SSV-1102A fails to close

adj.evidence: FT-GN-01 G-005; six-monthly SSV trip test records; separate impulse line

ipls.name: Separate impulse line for the monitor regulator, or an MP header high-pressure trip closing the inlet ESDV, SIL 1 (recommendation)
ipls.basis: Proposed – SIL 1 assumed; illustrative

others: PSV-1105 – Token relief valve (9.0 barg) to VS-1301 – lock-up creep / small leaks only, not sized for full regulator failure
PT-1106 – PRS outlet high-pressure alarm PAH-1106 (7.8 barg) with operator response
Regulator-run bypass valves car-sealed / locked closed (CSC register)
scenarios.notes: FT-GN-01 gives 2.0E-4 for the two overpressure protections together – more than the 0.0173 × 0.00763 = 1.3E-4 a LOPA would take for two independent layers, because of their common causes (gate G-003).

alarp.options: Separate impulse lines; MP header high-pressure trip; full-flow relief
alarp.decision: Further risk reduction is reasonably practicable – recommendation raised
alarp.justification: Recommendation raised for the separate impulse line / header trip

scenarios.result: Meets target (Safety); with proposed IPLs: Meets target – accepted IPLs only

scenarios.node: N06 – Rolling-mill reheat furnace fuel gas train and burner management
scenarios.deviation: Loss of flame with fuel gas still flowing
scenarios.cause: Burner flame-out with continued fuel supply
scenarios.consequence: Unburnt gas enters a furnace zone below auto-ignition temperature (start-up / low fire) – explosive mixture, furnace explosion: casing / door failure, fatalities on the furnace platforms

ie.desc: Burner flame-out with continued fuel supply
ie.basis: Burner flame-out with fuel still flowing – part of the FT-GN-03 demand, illustrative

enabling.desc: Furnace below auto-ignition temperature (start-up or low fire)
enabling.basis: About 10 % of operating time; a flame failure is revealed at once by the scanners

modifiers.desc: Probability that a person is present on the burner platform
modifiers.basis: Rounds about 17 h a week – CCPS ECCM (2014) Table 3.4

ipls.name: BMS-4000 – Reheat furnace BMS flame-failure shut-off (scanners BS-4010, logic BMS-4000, SSOVs XV-4002A/B)
ipls.basis: FT-GN-03 gate G-002 – BMS fails to shut off the fuel gas on flame failure (PFDavg from the fault tree)

adj.evidence: FT-GN-03 G-002; BMS SIL verification; scanner and SSOV test records
adj.conditions: Six-monthly scanner and safety shut-off valve tests

ipls.name: Furnace explosion relief doors; no-go zone around burner platforms during light-off
ipls.basis: Explosion relief doors and no-go zone – claimed in the HAZOP

adj.evidence: Marszal & Scharpf (2002) §9.4.6 – a layer that only lessens the consequence is not an IPL
adj.reason: Not specific – the doors limit the damage but do not prevent the furnace explosion

ipls.name: BMS upgrade to SIL 2: second flame scanner per burner, 1oo2 voting (recommendation)
ipls.basis: Proposed – additional factor 10 over the present BMS; illustrative

others: Furnace draught / post-purge removes unburnt gas through the stack before it can ignite
scenarios.notes: The explosion relief doors stay in the consequence analysis (they limit the damage) but are not credited as an IPL.

alarp.options: BMS upgrade; longer pre-purge; remote light-off
alarp.decision: Further risk reduction is reasonably practicable – recommendation raised
alarp.justification: Recommendation raised for the BMS upgrade

scenarios.result: SIL 1 needed (Safety, RRF 57.3); with proposed IPLs: Gap ≤ 10× – one more IPL or SIL 1 – accepted IPLs only
